preconditions: The viewport is 320 CSS pixels wide.

assistiveTechnologyTests.procedure: Follow the documented procedure and listen for the information under test.

title: Stacked table loses its column headers at narrow widths
description: Below 640 CSS pixels the attendance tables become stacked cards. The alpha variant hides the header row with display:none, so the data cells remain but their column headings are gone from the accessibility tree. The control keeps the header row available to assistive technology while hiding it visually.

relatedElements.note: The control keeps the header row in the accessibility tree at the same width.

expectedBehaviour: Responsive layouts keep the relationships between data cells and their headers available to assistive technology.
actualBehaviour: The header row is removed with display:none at narrow widths, leaving no column headers.
userImpact: Screen-reader users hear values such as 18 and 20 without being told whether they are bookings or capacity.

wcag.note: The visual and programmatic relationships between cells and headers diverge.
Information is lost when the content is presented at 320 CSS pixels.

detection.note: The defect only exists below the breakpoint, so a default-viewport scan reports a correct table.

observed.note: Page-level axe run with tags wcag2a, wcag2aa, wcag21a, wcag21aa and best-practice. No violation was reported; the control on the same page also passes.

manualTests: Set the viewport to 320 pixels wide and move through the attendance table in table navigation mode.

assertions: No column header roles exist in the alpha table at 320 pixels, while the control exposes three.
tests: tests/responsive-and-state.spec.js: keeps the alpha headers out of the accessibility tree at 320 pixels

reviewStatus.note: A Playwright regression test preserves the defective behaviour and its control. That is automated reproduction, not a manual or assistive-technology observation.
